podcast.title: Last Tour and Final Gig (December 2015)
podcast.body: The Wildabouts embarked on a tour at the end of 2015. On December 1, 2015, they played what would be Scott Weiland's final gig at Adelaide Hall in Toronto. Scott's third wife, Jamie, hoped he would get clean once this tour concluded. "On December 1st, 2015, he and The Wild Abuts pulled into Toronto...It would be his last gig."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Scott Weiland's Erratic Gigs (2015)
podcast.body: YouTube videos of The Wildabouts' gigs in 2015 hinted at Scott Weiland's erratic behavior on stage, raising concerns about his sobriety. "YouTube videos of Wild About Gigs hinted something erratic."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Tour Bus Death (December 3, 2015)
podcast.body: Scott Weiland died on The Wildabouts' tour bus on December 3, 2015, in Bloomington, Minnesota. He was found unresponsive by the band's tour manager in the back bedroom of the bus. "On Thursday, December 3rd, 2015, The Wild Abuts Tour Bus was in the parking lot of a country in and sweet hotel in Bloomington, Minnesota."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Scott Weiland's Last Band
podcast.body: The Wildabouts was the final band that Scott Weiland was a part of before his death on a tour bus in 2015. "And finally, there's Scott's last band, The Wild abouts, and his death on that tour bus."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Claimed Sobriety and Erratic Behavior (2013-2015)
xref.body: Although Scott Weiland claimed to have been drug-free for 13 years, there were numerous signs of his continued struggle with addiction, including YouTube videos of erratic performances with The Wildabouts. His third wife, Jamie, acknowledged his drinking but stated he promised to get clean after the 2015 tour. "Although Wyland claimed to have been off drugs for 13 years, there were plenty of indications that he was prone to slipping."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Death on Tour Bus (December 3, 2015)
xref.body: On December 1, 2015, The Wildabouts played in Toronto. On December 2, Weiland went out late with bassist Tommy Black. The next morning, December 3, Weiland woke around 9 AM on the tour bus, then returned to bed as the bus headed to Medina, Minnesota. When the bus arrived in Bloomington, Tommy Black found Weiland unresponsive and stiff around 8 PM after Weiland's wife, Jamie, requested the tour manager, Aaron Moller, check on him due to an unanswered text. Police pronounced him dead at the scene. "At around 8 pm, local time in Minnesota, Moller found Wyland lying in a fetal position on his left side. His eyes were half closed. His body was stiff."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Final Thanksgiving Dinner (November 25, 2015)
xref.body: On November 25, 2015, Scott Weiland had a romantic Thanksgiving dinner with his wife, Jamie, at an Italian restaurant called Maya Lino in New York. He seemed fine during this meal, which was the last time Jamie saw him alive. He was in the midst of a tour with his new band, The Wildabouts, and continued to drink heavily without perceiving it as a problem. "On November 25, 2015, Wyland had a romantic Thanksgiving dinner with his wife, Jamie. They went to an Italian restaurant in New York called Maya Lino."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Last Gig in Toronto (December 1, 2015)
xref.body: Scott Weiland and The Wildabouts performed at Adelaide Hall in Toronto on December 1, 2015. Weiland "did not look good" and conducted a couple of interviews before what would be his final performance. "It would be his last gig."
